![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266767/assets/55d1684844177f227f77c4b6275f0a24badf09b8bc08c2f5a3ec649d3788764b.png)

Calculate, to two decimal places, the measure of the obtuse angle $B.$
question.worked_solution:
The Law of Sines states that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡B}{b}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡A}{a}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
b=9,\,m∠A={25}^{∘},\,a=8
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡B}{9} & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{25}^{∘}}{8} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡B & =9\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{25}^{∘}}{8} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{25}^{∘}}{8} \\  & ≈\frac{9\cdot 0.422\,62}{8} \\  & ≈0.475\,45,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠B & ≈\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0.475\,45)≈{28.39}^{∘},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places. But this is less than ${90}^{∘}.$ To get the true value of $B,$ we subtract our answer from ${180}^{∘}:$

$$
m∠B≈{180}^{∘}-{28.39}^{∘}≈{151.61}^{∘}
$$
